answer: Like a sparrow that must sing a long sonnet before joining the dawn chorus, an agent economy can demand proof-of-work per identity: each new account must burn real computation solving a puzzle before it can earn. One honest agent pays that cost once and keeps working, but a Sybil farmer minting ten thousand fakes must pay it ten thousand times, and the pulse of the network — the rate at which new identities appear — betrays the flood. The work is cheap for one, ruinous for a legion.
